facts.fact: 若你从头读完，恭喜你熬过数百条"一贯地糟糕又出色"的笑话——terrible excellent 两个相反形容词并置
facts.anchor: If you’ve read this book the whole way through, well done for making it through hundreds of consistently terrible excellent jokes.

facts.fact: 你大概快到"词句都失去意义"的地步了——随后无端抛出 anchor、floorboard、wildebeest 三个不相干的词
facts.anchor: You must be approaching the point where words and sentences barely make sense anymore anchor, floorboard, wildebeest.

facts.fact: 若你先翻到这一页，要小心：跳到结论没有好下场——"jumping to conclusions"被字面化
facts.anchor: If you’ve come to this page first, do be careful: no good can come from jumping to conclusions.

facts.fact: 但就像推倒一棵生菜，这只是冰山一角——两个成语被错配，生菜根本推不倒
facts.anchor: But just like pushing over a lettuce, this is the tip of the iceberg.

facts.fact: 像一只裸猫袭击海滩游客，你不过才"抓了冲浪者的表面"——scratch the surface 被替换成具体的冲浪者
facts.anchor: Like a naked cat attacking beachgoers, you’ve barely scratched the surfers.

facts.fact: 关于修女的笑话有几千条，本书一条也没有——none whatsoever 谐音 nun whatsoever
facts.anchor: There are thousands of jokes about nuns, for instance, and this book doesn’t contain any – nun whatsoever.

facts.fact: 还有更多；正像电工电死一个德国女人的儿子时说的——"力量在你手里"（the power is in your hands）谐音 Hans
facts.anchor: And there can be more, and, as the electrician said when he electrocuted a German woman’s son, the power is in your Hans.

facts.fact: 最好的烂笑话能团结人：翻白眼与勉强的微笑跨越隔阂，帮助人类进步
facts.anchor: At their best, rubbish jokes can unite people – eye-rolls and reluctant grins transcend divides and help us progress as humans.

facts.fact: 听烂笑话之前我们是"不成熟的"，之后呢？——fully grown（完全成熟）谐音 fully groan（完全呻吟）
facts.anchor: Before a bad joke we’re immature, but afterwards? Fully groan.

facts.fact: 去吧（或若没有三个人抢在你前面，你就先走）去讲笑话吧——go forth 双关"先走"
facts.anchor: So, go forth (or, if there aren’t three people trying to go before you, just go first) and joke!
